rules.statement: Publish the protocol-error audit event from the single endpoint filter that wraps the OpenID endpoint group, and never from the individual sites that create or throw an error.
rules.why: Only a central funnel guarantees every error is covered, and covered exactly once. Publishing at each call site leaves a silent gap at the first forgotten site and can publish twice when an error is both created and thrown.
rules.check: Look for audit/event publish calls for error events added next to code that builds an OpenID error, returns error.AsHttpResult(), returns an error AuthorizationResult, or throws OpenIdException, rather than in the endpoint filter.

rules.statement: Publish audit events for state-changing successes at their call site, because no central funnel sees those responses.
rules.why: Successful responses such as a 204 never pass through an error funnel, so the call site is the only place that can record them.
rules.check: Look for a state-changing success path (create/update/delete/revoke) that has no audit publish at the call site, or that expects the error filter to record it.

rules.statement: When an error audit must happen once per request, enforce it with a constant sentinel key in HttpContext.Items, not by keying on the error instance's reference or hash.
rules.why: The invariant is one audit per errored request. Keying on the error object weakens that to one per object, and a hash key could wrongly suppress a different error.
rules.check: Look for dedup logic keyed on an error object, its reference or its hash code, or a non-constant Items key, used to stop duplicate audit publishes.

rules.statement: Wrap audit/event publishing so that a recorder failure is logged and swallowed and never changes the HTTP response.
rules.why: Auditing is an observation layer and must not affect the response the client gets.
rules.check: Look for audit or event publish calls on a request path that are not wrapped in a try/catch that logs the failure, so a recorder exception could escape or change the response.

rules.statement: On a thrown-error path, publish the audit from the exception's error before rendering the response, so the record survives if rendering throws.
rules.why: An eager publish means the audit record exists even when response rendering fails.
rules.check: Look at exception filters or handlers that publish the error audit only after rendering the error response, or only on a successful render.

rules.statement: Do not make a generic result wrapper implement an error marker interface. Decide whether a result is an error from the wrapped value at runtime, through a non-generic accessor, and keep marker interfaces for types that model an optional error by design.
rules.why: A wrapper that holds any response would advertise success results as error-bearing in the type system and pollute generic `where T : Marker` constraints.
rules.check: Look for a generic wrapper type (such as OpenIdResult<T>) that adds an error marker interface such as ISupportOpenIdError, or for filters that test error-ness by type instead of checking whether the wrapped response is an IOpenIdError.

rules.statement: A new non-protocol result type that carries an error must expose it to the error funnel, either by wrapping an IOpenIdError behind IOpenIdResult or by implementing ISupportOpenIdError.
rules.why: Otherwise the central filter cannot see the error and it goes unaudited.
rules.check: Look for new result types that carry an error but neither expose an IOpenIdError through IOpenIdResult nor implement ISupportOpenIdError.
